variableReadSpelling: VARIABLE-READ SPELLING (php, 2026-10-11). The `uses` targets in this file that name a `$variable` are BINDINGS, not declaration names: the analyzer spells a variable read as `<read source>\u0000<binding>` with `metadata.localBinding`, because a local/param/superglobal is never a published symbol and the BARE name let the store bind the read to an unrelated same-named declaration in another file. The defect and its counterfactual are in validation/m14/fixtures/php/local-read-phantom.mts; the whole-population effect is in docs/analyzers/history/php-lane-notes.md. What each row PINS (which read, from where, and how many) did not move.
rationale: R10 (#835) — the include-path spelling contract. The pre-R10 rule read the RAW TEXT of any `binary_expression` in an include/require position, so a concatenation with a runtime operand published a reconstructed EXPRESSION as the import module AND as a `references` target. Measured on phpmyadmin src/Git.php:97 (`include $this->baseDir . 'revision-info.php'`) and reproduced on this fixture by script/m14/tmp/php-include-prefix-rule.ts, which replays the OLD rule: it emitted `$this->baseDir.'/revision-info.php'`, `$dir.'/x.php'`, `{$dir}/interpolated.php` and `__DIR__.$suffix` — spellings carrying `$`, `->`, `.` and a quote that no php symbol can ever be named. The oracle derived its truth from the same rule, so BOTH sides agreed and every per-edge gate read clean; a target-spelling fixture that does not depend on the mirror is the only instrument that can hold it. The rule now requires every operand to be statically known: the six static paths below are unchanged (including `__DIR__.'/nested/'.'deeper.php'`, so the narrowing did not also narrow legitimate concatenation), and the four dynamic spellings are forbidden. `include $dir` (a bare variable) was ALREADY skipped pre-fix and is pinned here so it stays that way. The dynamic operands' own reads are still emitted — that is the point: a dynamic include loses the fabricated PATH, not the value reads. FOLLOW-UP, SAME ROUND (R10 census, 2026-09-23): the census convicted this lane on a target this fixture had DELIBERATELY pinned as correct — `references -> __DIR__.'/helpers.php'`, the raw source text of a fully static concatenation. The earlier decision recorded that a static concatenation was legitimate (it is) but then rendered it as source syntax, and the census's standing question is a different one: is the target spelled the way the lane spells a symbol at all? A quote is not. Measured live on phpunit's autoloaders — `references -> "__DIR__.'/src/DeprecatedClass.php"` in tests/end-to-end/regression/6778/bootstrap.php, 4 sites in a 300-file draw of 4,096 php files — and on both php corpora the census read php as an OO lane with UNRULED separator vocabulary (`references|'`), against the owner standard's zero target for OO lanes. The rule now composes the operands' VALUES instead of returning the node's text: `__DIR__ . '/helpers.php'` publishes `__DIR__/helpers.php`, `FILE_PREFIX . '/config.php'` publishes `FILE_PREFIX/config.php`, and the two-operand case publishes `__DIR__/nested/deeper.php`. Nothing is narrowed: all six static paths still emit, the four dynamic shapes are still refused, and the phase that decides staticness is untouched — only the rendering was wrong. The pre-fix spellings are forbidden above. RELABELLED 2026-10-23 (R3, no grammar change): the six static paths are emitted as `part_of` rows, not `imports`, with `meta.partRole: "library"` on each and the written directive form kept row by row as `meta.includeType` — a file-level directive that names a path and creates no module binding is what `part_of` was added to spell, and the ImportInfo directive list is still published (so a consumer reading a file's includes loses nothing). The spelling rule this fixture exists for did not move: same six targets, same four refusals, same `__DIR__`/`FILE_PREFIX` composition.

expectRelationships.note: 2026-10-23 relabel (R3, no grammar change): a file-level directive that names a path and creates no module binding is `part_of`, not `imports`. partRole is MANDATORY and is `library` because php has only the host form of Dart's two roles — the file carrying the directive includes the part. The written form is kept per row as evidence, which is what makes the include/require/include_once/require_once SPLIT measured rather than lumped.
